q: Williams' classification of SFTs by strong shift equivalence states that two SFTs (with adjacency matrices A, B) are conjugate iff:
opts: A and B have the same determinant
A and B are strongly shift equivalent (related by a chain of elementary equivalences R, S with RS=A, SR=B)
A and B have the same spectrum
A and B have the same size
exp: Williams' theorem (1973): SFTs defined by non-negative integer matrices A, B are topologically conjugate iff A and B are strongly shift equivalent (SSE). Checking SSE is algorithmically undecidable in general; shift equivalence (a weaker algebraic relation) is decidable but not equivalent to SSE.
